newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreigners net Japan bond buying hits record high.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners net Japan bond buying hits record high.

text.p: Net purchases of Japanese bonds by foreigners hit a record high of 1.4196 trillion yen in September, surpassing the previous record of 780.1 billion set in March 1995, a Ministry of Finance official said on Monday.
"According to market sources, heavy trading in the futures market, mainly led by U.S. and European fund operators, was the main factor that pushed up the figures sharply," he said.

In September, a record large 2.34 trillion yen cash bond delivery for the September Japanese government bond futures contract was made. Of the total, one U.S. brokerage took delivery of an estimated 1.8 trillion yen in cash bonds.

Bond traders said that the U.S. brokerage had tried to corner the market by holding large long open interest in the September JGB contract, while it had heavily borrowed the cheapest cash JGBs at the same time. The short-squeezing in the yen bond market was the main reason behind the large yen bond purchases by foreigners in September, they said.

The MOF official said that foreigners' purchases were also active in September after expectations of an imminent credit tightening in Japan faded away. Rallies in the U.S. bond market also helped boost the purchases.
